edit_summary: Fail to retarget parser stack operands that point to the first byte of a reallocated CFF2 blend stack.
root_cause: Parser stack operands may point into subFont->blend_stack; after FT_QREALLOC moves that buffer, every operand in the old buffer range including the base address must be adjusted by the relocation offset.
effect_path: A first blend result stored at blend_stack_old remains on the parser stack, a later blend grows the blend buffer and moves it, and cff_parse_fixed reads that stale operand pointer while computing the next blended value.
guard_p1: A CFF2 dict or charstring blend produces a result whose encoded bytes begin exactly at the current blend_stack base.
guard_p2: A subsequent blend in the same parser stack forces FT_QREALLOC to move the blend buffer before the old result is consumed.
hardness_reason: The freed identity crosses allocator relocation and parser-stack state; operands inside the old buffer but not at the base are still adjusted, and no-reallocation blends are safe neighbors.
naturalness_reason: Off-by-one range checks around pointer-retargeting after realloc are natural in compact interpreter state management.
explanation: Parser stack operands may point into subFont->blend_stack; after FT_QREALLOC moves that buffer, every operand in the old buffer range including the base address must be adjusted by the relocation offset. A first blend result stored at blend_stack_old remains on the parser stack, a later blend grows the blend buffer and moves it, and cff_parse_fixed reads that stale operand pointer while computing the next blended value.
cause_site_expected: src/cff/cffload.c cff_blend_doBlend reallocates subFont->blend_stack with FT_QREALLOC
effect_site_expected: src/cff/cffload.c cff_blend_doBlend calls cff_parse_fixed on parser stack operands from the old blend buffer

naturalness_reason: Comparator slips in tree walkers over flat parser tokens are natural when size encodes child presence rather than byte length.

neighbor_case: the same key has a primitive or string value, so key->size > 0 and t + 1 + j is valid
oob_site_expected: recursive dump(js, t + 1 + j, ...) dereferences a token beyond p.toknext

edit_summary: Store code and raw-HTML block lines with the normal MD_LINE layout while their block type still dispatches as verbatim content.
root_cause: MD_BLOCK_CODE and MD_BLOCK_HTML require MD_VERBATIMLINE records because later verbatim rendering reads an indentation field in addition to beg/end.
effect_path: Block analysis records a code or raw-HTML block with type MD_BLOCK_CODE or MD_BLOCK_HTML, but md_add_line_into_current_block appends MD_LINE records; md_process_leaf_block later dispatches by the block type and casts the following bytes to MD_VERBATIMLINE.
guard_p1: The document contains a fenced, indented-code, or raw-HTML block whose current_block type is one of the verbatim layouts.
guard_p2: The block reaches md_process_all_blocks, which trusts the block type to select md_process_code_block_contents or md_process_verbatim_block_contents.
hardness_reason: The broken layout invariant crosses block construction and the later rendering pass over the packed block byte arena; ordinary paragraph blocks remain safe because they really use MD_LINE records.
naturalness_reason: A boolean condition typo in a shared layout discriminator is a realistic type/layout confusion in packed C parser arenas.
explanation: MD_BLOCK_CODE and MD_BLOCK_HTML require MD_VERBATIMLINE records because later verbatim rendering reads an indentation field in addition to beg/end. Block analysis records a code or raw-HTML block with type MD_BLOCK_CODE or MD_BLOCK_HTML, but md_add_line_into_current_block appends MD_LINE records; md_process_leaf_block later dispatches by the block type and casts the following bytes to MD_VERBATIMLINE.
actual_type: MD_LINE records appended after a verbatim block header
expected_type: MD_VERBATIMLINE records for MD_BLOCK_CODE and MD_BLOCK_HTML
wrong_layout_effect: Verbatim rendering reads the missing indent field and the block iterator advances using sizeof(MD_VERBATIMLINE) over MD_LINE storage.

edit_summary: Let capture retry matching measure its inner subject length from the wrong base cursor.
root_cause: The capture retry loop starts the inner match at s + j, so the length passed to doh must subtract both the pre-capture offset j and the retry shrink j2.
effect_path: For a capture reached after leading subject bytes, the modified length is too large by j and lets nested alternation or literal matching read past the provided subject slice.
guard_p1: A regex has a capture after at least one literal byte and a following suffix that forces capture retry attempts near the end of the subject.
guard_p2: The neighboring regex starts the capture at subject offset zero, or the subject has enough trailing bytes to cover the overstated length.
expected_crash: out-of-bounds subject read during recursive capture retry
hardness_reason: The bad length is introduced in capture retry bookkeeping and consumed by nested doh/bar recursion, so finding it requires tracking both regex and subject cursors.
naturalness_reason: Cursor-base mixups are natural in recursive regex engines because the pointer and length parameters are carried separately.
explanation: The retry loop shrinks the candidate capture but keeps the same s + j base pointer. Dropping the j subtraction gives nested matching a length that extends beyond the subject slice.
boundary_invariant: the length paired with s + j must not exceed s_len - j, and retry j2 must further reduce it
boundary_case: capture begins at j > 0 and retry reaches the end of the subject slice

root_cause: Large-window Brotli keeps the format-level 62-bit distance alphabet but must cap the decoded alphabet to BROTLI_MAX_ALLOWED_DISTANCE before distance offsets are converted into int distance_code.
